distinctions_drawn: Material object (living organism) vs. Abstract object (mereological sum)
Synchronic identity (at a time) vs. Diachronic identity (across time)
explicit_definitions_given: DAUP: For any object X, any arbitrary selection of its proper parts constitutes a proper part of X.
Proper part: A part not identical to the whole.
D-minus: The mereological sum of Descartes' parts excluding the leg.

objections_raised: The semantic ambiguity of 'Descartes' (material vs. abstract) may break the transitivity of identity.
The identity conditions for material organisms may differ from those of abstract sums, invalidating the reductio.

summary_of_core_decisions: The text's blueprint is a classic analytic dialectic. It establishes a thesis (DAUP), introduces a powerful antithesis (van Inwagen's reductio), and then isolates a specific defensive strategy (semantic disambiguation). The essay's core methodological move is to test whether the material/abstract distinction can successfully sever the logical chain of the reductio, specifically by challenging the transitivity of identity or the proper-parthood relation. The ultimate goal is to determine if the semantic escape route is a genuine solution or a mere verbal dodge.
